subject: Information Theory
title: Transform Coding
description: Learn Transform Coding in one minute.

hook.text: JPEG doesn't compress pixels directly. It transforms them into frequencies first—then compresses those.

buildup.text: Transform coding converts data into a domain where energy is concentrated in fewer coefficients.

discovery.text: The DCT turns an 8×8 pixel block into frequency components. Most energy sits in the low frequencies.

twist.text: High-frequency coefficients carry fine detail. Zeroing them out barely changes the image but saves lots of data.

climax.text: DCT, wavelet, and Fourier transforms all share this idea: compress in the domain where things are sparse.

punchline.text: Change the domain. Make compression easy.

quiz.question: Why does JPEG use the discrete cosine transform?
options: To concentrate energy into fewer coefficients for easier compression
